subject: Chemistry
q: Which intermolecular forces predominate in liquid ethyl acetate?
options: Hydrogen bonding and London dispersion forces
London dispersion forces, dipole–dipole forces and hydrogen bonding
London dispersion forces and dipole–dipole forces
hint: Identify whether ethyl acetate is polar and whether it contains an O–H, N–H or F–H bond.
solution: Every molecule exhibits London dispersion forces. The polar ester group gives ethyl acetate a permanent molecular dipole, so dipole–dipole forces also act. Pure ethyl acetate has no hydrogen attached to O, N or F and therefore cannot hydrogen-bond with itself. Hence the predominant forces are London dispersion and dipole–dipole forces.
